# Code pipelines

Start code pipelines, wait for them, and read them.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [Code pipelines](../../../concepts/code-pipelines.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`CodePipelineAwait`](#codepipelineawait) | Waits until a code pipeline run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run. |
| [`CodePipelineGet`](#codepipelineget) | Returns a code pipeline run as it is now, without waiting for it. |
| [`CodePipelineList`](#codepipelinelist) | Returns every code pipeline run in your tenant that hasn't ended yet. |
| [`CodePipelineStart`](#codepipelinestart) | Starts a code pipeline run and returns its id straight away, without waiting for it to finish. |

### CodePipelineAwait

Waits until a code pipeline run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run.

```c
jsonObject CodePipelineAwait(guid id)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `guid` | The run's id, as [`CodePipelineStart`](#codepipelinestart) returned it. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The ended run, as a JSON object.

It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own: it waits as long as the run takes. A pipeline can take hours, and its own time limits still apply; give an app that waits for one a long enough time limit of its own. A run waiting for an answer to an agent's question (`HumanInteractionRequired`) hasn't ended, so the wait goes on. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

The run is a JSON object, the same one the API returns for a code pipeline run. Its most useful fields are `status`; `variables`, each `{ name, value }`: every step's result, under the step's output variable name, and the values hooks set; `failureDetails` and `failureReason`, why it failed; `phases`, each phase with its steps as they ran; `outputFiles`; `inputs`; and `id`, `dateStarted`, `dateEnded`, `executionTime`, `parentProcessId` and `rootProcessId`. Keys and tokens are never included.

Check `status` before you use the result: a run that failed ends the wait too. Fails with `CodePipeline process … not found` when your tenant has no code pipeline run with that id.

### CodePipelineGet

Returns a code pipeline run as it is now, without waiting for it.

```c
jsonObject CodePipelineGet(string processId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `string` | The code pipeline run's id. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The run, as a JSON object.

The run is the JSON object [`CodePipelineAwait`](#codepipelineawait) describes. While it is going, its `status` is `New`, `Running`, `HumanInteractionRequired` (an agent asked a question) or `HumanInteractionComplete`; once it has ended, `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Fails with `Invalid process ID format: …` when `processId` isn't an id, and `Not found` when your tenant has no code pipeline run with that id.

### CodePipelineList

Returns every code pipeline run in your tenant that hasn't ended yet.

```c
jsonArray CodePipelineList()
```

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of code pipeline runs.

It lists the runs in every namespace, whoever started them. Each element of the JSON array is a run as [`CodePipelineAwait`](#codepipelineawait) describes it.

### CodePipelineStart

Starts a code pipeline run and returns its id straight away, without waiting for it to finish.

```c
string CodePipelineStart(string namespaceName, string pipelineName, jsonObject startRequestJson)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the pipeline is in. |
| `pipelineName` | `string` | The pipeline's name. |
| `startRequestJson` | `jsonObject` | The start request, as a JSON object in the form the API's code pipeline start takes: `inputs`, an array of `{ "name": "request", "value": "…" }`; `repos`, the git repositories to work on, with credentials that can push; and optional settings such as `agentOverrides`, `credentials`, `vfsMounts`, `inputFileIds` and `launchIntentId`. Pass `"{}"` for a pipeline that takes no inputs and no repositories. |

**Returns** `string`: The new run's id.

Unlike most calls, the namespace is an argument of its own, and is required. The run uses the pipeline's latest enabled version. Wait for it with [`CodePipelineAwait`](#codepipelineawait).

The run is a child of this app run: its `parentProcessId` is this run, and it shares this run's `rootProcessId`. It uses this run's credential stack when this run's start chose one, and this run's time limits and web settings for any the request leaves out.

Give the request a `launchIntentId` of your own to make a retry safe: a start with an id already used returns the run that start made, rather than starting another.

Fails when the pipeline or its namespace doesn't exist (`Code pipeline '…' was not found in namespace '…'.`), with `Invalid startRequestJson: …` when the request doesn't parse, with `Invalid CodePipeline start parameters: …` when it is refused (an input missing, say), and when your plan refuses the start.
